testedDecision: Whether the nurse should immediately activate qualified interpreter services and document the language-access plan rather than gesturing, using the son, or waiting for rounds
reason: The exposed postoperative day 1 note already documents the nurse's conclusion that a certified Mandarin interpreter is needed for comprehensive discharge teaching, which is the keyed action stated forward in time. Postoperative day 2 then shows a certified interpreter producing successful teach-back while English handouts and family telephone interpretation are shown failing, retiring three distractors before the learner reasons. The Chinese stage text carries the same disclosures at the same points

testedDecision: Whether a failed teach-back requires halting discharge readiness and arranging certified interpreter-supported teaching rather than repeating English materials, deferring to home health, or using the son
reason: Postoperative day 2 narrates the case performing the keyed action itself, with a certified in-person Mandarin interpreter delivering teaching that the client then repeats accurately. That same exposure shows the client was not discharged on postoperative day 1 and that the son was never used as the clinical interpreter, which retires both deferral distractors. Postoperative day 3 confirms discharge happened only after interpreter-supported teaching succeeded

testedDecision: Which barrier-directed actions must precede discharge when mobility, language, support, referral, and renal-anticoagulant concerns remain unresolved despite medical stability
reason: Postoperative day 2 enacts the keyed option set nearly one to one, showing case management interviewing the client and initiating the home health referral, certified interpreter teaching, and physical therapy completing walker, stair, and equipment planning. It also shows the surgeon writing the discharge order only for the following morning pending nursing confirmation of readiness, which confirms the reassessment option and refutes the proceed-with-discharge distractor. Postoperative day 3 restates that every identified barrier was resolved before the client left

testedDecision: Whether each proposed action around rivaroxaban with a declining eGFR falls inside nursing scope, including prescriber notification and refusing an independent medication hold
reason: The exposed postoperative day 3 handoff lists renal-function trend, anticoagulant adherence, and bleeding surveillance as what the nurse actually communicated, restating the handoff matrix row almost verbatim as correct. That same note shows the client discharged still taking rivaroxaban with an improved creatinine, cueing that an independent nurse hold was not the appropriate row. The prescriber-notification and food-requirement rows stay knowledge-driven, so the leak is partial yet still material

testedDecision: Which discharge-plan actions close the gap between the client naming warning signs and actually reaching the surgeon despite an English-only office phone system
reason: Postoperative day 3 performs all four keyed actions in narrative form, calling the surgeon's office to request a Mandarin interpreter for follow-up, naming the son as the communication contact within the SBAR handoff, and supplying Mandarin written materials with agency phone numbers. A learner reading that exposed note can transcribe the answer set instead of reasoning about functional access barriers. The Chinese stage text lists the identical four actions, so the exposure is equally available in both languages
